Package neqsim.process.dynamics

Class BDFIntegrator

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.dynamics.BDFIntegrator
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, IntegratorStrategy
public class BDFIntegrator extends Object implements IntegratorStrategy
BDF-1 (backward differentiation formula of order 1, i.e. implicit Euler) integrator: 
   x_{n+1} = x_n + dt · f(t_{n+1}, x_{n+1})

Solved by Newton iteration. Implicit Euler is L-stable and well suited for stiff thermal, inventory, and pressure-dynamics problems that arise in dynamic process simulation (vessel pressure decay, large-tank temperature dynamics, slow level loops).

The Jacobian ∂f/∂x is approximated by a central finite difference with step max(jacobianEps, jacobianEps · |x|). Newton stops when both the update and implicit-equation residual satisfy the configured tolerance. Newton non-convergence is fail-loud by default; an explicit-Euler fallback is available only through the deliberately opt-in setExplicitEulerFallbackEnabled(boolean) compatibility switch. A fallback is never reported as a converged BDF step.

This class remains a scalar BDF-1 foundation. It is not a vector sparse BDF or DAE solver and must not be used as evidence of plant-wide stiff/DAE qualification.

    • lastStepFellBack

      public boolean lastStepFellBack()
      Indicates whether the most recent step(double, double, neqsim.process.dynamics.IntegratorStrategy.Slope, double) call used the explicitly enabled Euler compatibility fallback.

      A fallback means the requested BDF step did not converge. It is therefore not a successful implicit step and must not be counted as stiff-integration qualification evidence.

      Returns:
      true when the last step used explicit Euler after BDF non-convergence

    • lastStepConverged

      Returns:
      true only when the implicit BDF equation converged

    • setExplicitEulerFallbackEnabled

      public void setExplicitEulerFallbackEnabled(boolean enabled)
      Enables or disables the legacy explicit-Euler fallback after BDF Newton non-convergence.

      The default is false: non-convergence throws IllegalStateException so a physical-step coordinator can reject and restore the step. Enabling this switch is an explicit compatibility choice; the returned Euler state is marked by lastStepFellBack() and lastStepConverged() remains false.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to return an explicit-Euler compatibility step after BDF failure

    • isExplicitEulerFallbackEnabled

      public boolean isExplicitEulerFallbackEnabled()
      Returns whether the explicit-Euler compatibility fallback is enabled.
      Returns:
      true when fallback is enabled
